user.title: NeverDry — Sensors & Model
user.description: Select your weather sensors and configure the ET model parameters.

data_description.rain_sensor: Rain gauge or weather station precipitation sensor
data_description.rain_sensor_type: How your rain sensor reports precipitation. Event-based: mm per event (tipping bucket, recommended). Daily total: cumulative mm since midnight (weather station)
data_description.alpha: Used **only** by the Simple (linear) water-balance method: it converts a temperature excess into millimetres of evapotranspiration, so it carries everything that method does not measure. Hargreaves-Samani and Penman-Monteith compute that from physics and ignore this box entirely — if one of those is running, changing this has no effect. Calibrate it on a zone in full sun and open ground: on a shaded zone you would bake that zone's shade into a site-wide constant and every other zone would inherit it. Per-zone differences belong to the site exposure of each zone, not here. Start at 0.22 and adjust after watching your garden for a week
data_description.t_base: Used **only** by the Simple (linear) water-balance method: the temperature below which it assumes no evapotranspiration at all, which is what keeps a straight line from predicting water loss on a cold day. Hargreaves-Samani carries its own fixed constant instead and ignores this box; Penman-Monteith does not need one. So if either is running, changing this has no effect
data_description.d_max: Upper limit for the deficit index
data_description.humidity_sensor: Optional. Unlocks Penman-Monteith together with wind and radiation.
data_description.wind_speed_sensor: Optional. Unlocks Penman-Monteith together with humidity and radiation.
data_description.net_radiation_sensor: Optional. A pyranometer reading in W/m2. The net radiation FAO-56 uses is computed from it, so it is not asked for.
data_description.et_method: Leave on Automatic unless you want to pin one method. A method whose sensors you have not declared is refused, and the error says which one is missing. The method actually in use is shown by the *Water balance method* sensor on the NeverDry device.

zone.title: Add irrigation zone
zone.description: Configure zone #{zone_count}. You can add more zones after this.

data_description.name: Display name for this zone (e.g., Vegetable Garden, Lawn)

ground_and_location.name: Ground and location
ground_and_location.description: What is watered here: how big the zone is, what grows in it, and how exposed it is.

data.kc: Custom crop coefficient Kc (overrides plant family)

data_description.area_m2: Surface area of this irrigation zone in square meters
data_description.plant_family: Sets the seasonal Kc curve for what grows here. Pick Custom to enter one fixed Kc below.
data_description.kc: Used only when the plant family is Custom. With any other family the seasonal curve applies and this field is ignored.
data_description.exposure: How much sun and wind this zone gets compared to an open site. Multiplies the Kc, so the zone keeps its seasonal curve instead of being frozen at one fixed value. Pick Custom to enter your own factor below.
data_description.microclimate_factor: Used only when the exposure is Custom. Range 0.1–1.5; above 1.0 for zones that dry faster than open ground.
data_description.vwc_sensor:
Optional. A probe buried in this zone, about a third of the root depth down and midway between two emitters. On its own it is shown beside the zone's figures and nothing else changes. Give it the root depth below and this zone waters by what its soil says.

**The sensor must report on a 0-100 scale**, 0 for dry soil and 100 for wet, which is what garden moisture probes publish. A sensor on any other scale is not supported and its readings are ignored.

**That scale is used uncalibrated, fixed at 0-100 taken at face value:** 0 is treated as the driest soil a plant can work in and 100 as a full one. Real probes are calibrated at the factory against dry air and open water, and neither of those is a state soil is ever in, so a full soil does not actually read 100. The millimetres this produces are therefore out by a factor nobody has measured, usually on the high side, which means watering somewhat more than needed rather than leaving a zone dry. If that matters to you, the reasoning and what would fix it are written up here: https://github.com/never-dry/NeverDry/blob/main/docs/design/soil-moisture-model.md
data_description.root_depth_m: Depth of the root zone the probe above speaks for, and the one number here that no table holds: a lawn, a hedge and a pot differ by a factor of four on the same ground. Fill it in and this zone waters by its probe instead of the weather estimate. Leave it and the probe stays a reading shown beside the estimate. The probe's 0-100 reading is read as how much of the water this soil can actually hold is still there, so the depth and the soil below are what turn it into millimetres.
data_description.field_capacity: Only read when the soil type above is Custom. The water content this soil holds after it has finished draining, as a fraction: roughly 0.15 for sand, 0.25 for loam, 0.35 for clay. Used for the weather estimate; a zone on Custom soil cannot be watered by its probe.
data_description.soil_type: Optional. What this zone's ground is made of. It supplies how much water the soil holds and how much of that a plant can reach, so you do not have to know either number. Left on Automatic a medium soil is assumed, which is fair for most gardens and is said out loud when you save. Custom supplies only one of the two, so a probe cannot water a Custom-soil zone: pick a named soil for that.

valve_and_pipe.name: Valve and pipe
valve_and_pipe.description: What waters it: the valve, how delivery is measured, and the irrigation system.

data.flow_meter_sensor: Delivery measurement sensor — counter or flow rate (flow meter mode only)
data.volume_entity: Volume target entity (volume dosing mode only)

data_description.valve: The switch entity that controls this zone's irrigation valve. Leave empty for monitoring mode (no valve)
data_description.delivery_mode: How your valve delivers water. Estimated flow: simple on/off valve, duration calculated from flow rate. Flow meter: valve with a flow sensor, closes at target volume. Volume preset: smart valve that accepts a volume target and closes itself.
data_description.flow_rate_lpm: The sum of the rated output of everything this zone waters — sprinklers, drippers, micro-sprayers — in liters per hour (gal/h in imperial). Take it from the emitters' rating or your irrigation plan; you do not need to measure it. It is what the zone was built to deliver, and it is required: without it there is no way to turn a volume into a watering duration. What the zone actually delivers is measured separately from real sessions, and the gap between the two is worth watching.
data_description.flow_meter_sensor: Either kind works, and NeverDry tells them apart by the unit of measurement. A cumulative counter (L, gal, m³) is read before and after the run and the difference is the volume delivered — the more accurate of the two, because it does not depend on reporting frequency. An instantaneous flow rate (L/min, L/h, m³/h, gal/min, gal/h) is integrated over the run instead, so how often your valve reports its flow sets how good the number is. Required when the delivery mode is the one with a flow meter.
data_description.volume_entity: Number entity on the smart valve that accepts a volume target in liters. Required when the delivery mode leaves the dosing to the valve.
data_description.system_type: Sets the zone's efficiency (drip 0.92, micro-sprinklers 0.80, pop-up 0.68, manual 0.55). Pick Custom to enter your own below.
data_description.efficiency: Used only when the system type is Custom. With any other type this field is ignored and the form will tell you so.
data_description.delivery_timeout: Maximum time to wait for a measured or self-dosed delivery before forcing the valve closed (safety limit).

scheduling.name: Scheduling
scheduling.description: When it waters: on a timer, on a deficit threshold, or only on request.

data_description.irrigation_time: Time of day when NeverDry checks the deficit and irrigates if above threshold. Leave empty to disable automatic scheduling
data_description.threshold: Deficit level that triggers automatic irrigation for this zone

options.auto: Automatic — the best method my sensors support

reset.name: Reset deficit
reset.description: Reset the soil water deficit to zero (typically called after irrigation completes).

reset_yearly_rain.name: Reset yearly rain
reset_yearly_rain.description: Reset the year-to-date rain total to zero (system-wide). The total is a single value shared by every zone's "Rain Yearly" sensor and normally resets on its own on 1 January. Use this to clear a wrong value, for example after switching rain sensor type, without waiting for the new year or reinstalling. Historical statistics are left untouched.

reset_yearly_water.name: Reset yearly water
reset_yearly_water.description: Reset the year-to-date irrigated-water total to zero for every zone. Each zone keeps its own yearly counter and normally resets on 1 January; this clears them all at once. The lifetime total delivered per zone and historical statistics are left untouched.

irrigate_zone.name: Irrigate zone
irrigate_zone.description: Start irrigation for a single zone. How the water is measured depends on the zone's delivery mode: on a timer, at a volume read from a water meter, or by handing a volume target to a smart valve that doses it itself.

zone_name.name: Zone name
zone_name.description: The name of the zone to irrigate (as configured).

irrigate_all.name: Irrigate all zones
irrigate_all.description: Irrigate all configured zones sequentially. Each zone uses its own delivery mode. A pause between zones allows pressure stabilization. The deficit is reset after all zones complete.

stop.name: Emergency stop
stop.description: Immediately close all irrigation valves. Use this to abort an irrigation cycle in progress.

stop_zone.name: Stop zone
stop_zone.description: Stop irrigation for a single zone, leaving the other zones running.

zone_name.name: Zone name
zone_name.description: The zone whose irrigation should be stopped.

mark_irrigated.name: Mark zone as irrigated
mark_irrigated.description: Record that a zone was watered by hand, so the model credits the water and stops asking for it. Use it after watering with a hose.

zone_name.name: Zone name
zone_name.description: The zone to mark as irrigated. Leave empty for all zones.

set_deficit.name: Set deficit
set_deficit.description: Set a zone's water deficit to a chosen value. Use it to correct the model after something it could not see, such as a heavy manual watering or a stretch with the rain sensor offline.

deficit_mm.name: Deficit (mm)
deficit_mm.description: Target deficit value in mm. Must be >= 0.

zone_name.name: Zone name
zone_name.description: The zone to update. Leave empty to update all zones.

reset_valve.name: Reset valve (unlock maintenance)
reset_valve.description: Bring a zone out of maintenance and let it water again. A zone is put into maintenance after repeated valve failures, and it stays there until someone has looked at the valve.

zone_name.name: Zone name
zone_name.description: The zone whose valve should be unlocked.

test_valve.name: Valve test (supervised)
test_valve.description: Open one zone's valve for a set time and measure what it actually delivers, so the measured rate can be compared with the one the zone was built for. Watch the zone while it runs.

duration_min.name: Duration
duration_min.description: Minutes to keep the valve open. One minute makes for an unreliable measurement: a counter that steps in whole litres barely moves in that time, and a rate computed from one or two steps describes the counter's resolution rather than the zone. Longer runs cost water but are the only way to measure a slow zone at all.

common.notification_unreachable_passive_body: Zone {zone} valve has not responded for {duration}.
common.notification_unreachable_at_irrigation_t: Valve not responding at irrigation time
common.notification_unreachable_at_irrigation_b: Could not start irrigation for zone {zone}: valve not responding ({reason}). Check the valve battery and the Zigbee mesh before retrying.
common.notification_flow_meter_dead_body: Zone {zone} water meter is not reporting ({detail}). Irrigation ran on the design flow rate instead of being skipped, so the volume is estimated rather than measured. Check the meter entity: a silent meter is far more likely than a dry pipe.
common.notification_delivery_uncredited_title: Water delivered could not be credited
common.notification_delivery_uncredited_body: Zone {zone} delivered water that could not be measured ({detail}) and has no design flow rate to estimate it with, so its deficit is unchanged and the zone will be watered again on the next cycle. Set the zone's design flow rate, or fix the meter.
common.notification_stuck_open_title: Valve stuck open: shut off mains water
common.notification_stuck_open_body: Zone {zone} valve switch reports OFF but water is still flowing ({flow}). The integration has already attempted recovery and triggered an emergency stop for every other zone. **Manually shut off your main water valve now** and inspect the affected valve before resuming irrigation.
common.notification_leak_detected_body: Flow detected while every valve is closed. Last reading: {flow}.
common.notification_irrigation_ineffective_body: Zone {zone}: soil moisture did not rise after the last irrigation.
common.notification_model_drift_body: Zone {zone}: moisture/model correlation has dropped to {correlation}.
common.notification_water_me_now_body: Zone {zone}: deficit {deficit} above threshold; water by hand.
common.notification_watchdog_triggered_body: Zone {zone} valve was open for more than {duration_min} min with no close command received. NeverDry forced it closed as a safety measure. Check that the automation or delivery logic is working correctly.

soil_probe_needs_a_zone.title: NeverDry: which zone is the soil probe in?

confirm.title: Which zone is the probe in?
confirm.description:
The soil moisture probe `{probe}` is declared for the whole installation, so every zone is currently reading it. A probe measures one patch of soil, with one kind of planting above it and its own watering history — its reading is not transferable to a zone watered independently.

Tell NeverDry which zone it is buried in. Nothing has changed in the meantime: your zones are behaving exactly as before, and will keep doing so until you answer.

data.zone: Which zone is the probe in?

data_description.zone: The chosen zone will measure its deficit from the probe. The other zones go back to estimating it, which is what a probe in somebody else's soil could never tell them.
